task: Horizon 15 of agent-agnostic-browser-bridge: build a bounded, reversible "render the sandbox tab" primitive via CDP Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled (feasibility probe first), then ship full-page (beyond-viewport) screenshots as captureTab's one new consumer, reusing the h14 downscale ladder unchanged.

analysis.objective: Build a bounded, reversible "render the sandbox tab" primitive — contingent on a live-Chrome feasibility probe of CDP Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled — that gives the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab a real render pass for the duration of one capture and then restores the unfocused-tab invariant, and wire it to exactly one consumer: a new full-page (beyond-viewport) mode on captureTab reusing horizon 14's scale-only PNG downscale ladder.
analysis.successDefinition: Done means all hold: (1) a live-Chrome feasibility probe against the running extension has recorded in discoveries.md whether Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled actually restores a render pass on the unfocused sandbox tab enough for captureBeyondViewport to return non-blank beyond-viewport pixels within the 15s withDebuggerSession cap — and if it refutes that, the horizon replans rather than wiring anything permanent; (2) a render-the-tab primitive exists that is bounded (time-boxed to one capture), reversible (focus-emulation / render state is disabled and the pre-call unfocused state restored on every exit path including error and timeout), and leaves no orphaned debugger session or lingering focus-emulation after it returns; (3) captureTab gains a full-page mode via the existing in-place mode field with PAGE_ACTIONS still 20, across the full parity surface (protocol/actions.ts, protocol/types.ts, extension handler raw+guarded maps, tool-catalog.ts, mcp/server.ts, README, hardcoded count/list tests); (4) an oversized full-page result is driven down horizon 14's existing scale-only PNG ladder and returns the h14 too-large outcome (reason 'too-large' + floor/attempts) at the give-up floor, with no new JPEG rung and no new failure reason; (5) tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and vitest all pass for tools/chrome-bridge with unit tests covering the primitive's restore-on-every-path behavior and the full-page ladder; (6) a mandatory fresh-session live-Chrome head-to-head against the running extension captures a real beyond-viewport page in the unfocused sandbox tab, cross-checks returned pixel dimensions against measured scrollHeight/width, confirms the tab is unfocused again afterward, and is recorded dated in discoveries.md (a stale-MCP-catalog retry in a post-rebuild session is expected and not a failure); (7) boky's extension, bridge, and verify pipeline keep passing unchanged.
assumptions: The horizon-9 lift of the CDP Runtime.evaluate ban, plus horizon-6/13 use of chrome.debugger Page.captureScreenshot, is broad enough authorization to call one additional experimental CDP Emulation method for this primitive; it does not reopen the still-deferred persistent-CDP-session or trusted-Input.dispatch* decisions.
The primitive continues to use per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach (horizon-10 decision) — enable focus emulation, capture, disable and detach — not a new persistent session.
Full-page capture is the single consumer this horizon ships; virtualized/lazy-content reads and trusted CDP input remain blocked behind the same primitive and are deferred.

The full-page result reuses CaptureTabImageResult / CaptureTabFailureResult exactly as horizon 14 left them (appliedScale/attempts on success, floor/attempts on too-large); no new fields or reason members.
The 1_200_000 base64-char too-large ceiling carried from horizon 13/14 is used as-is; empirically re-measuring the true AI-client image-block reject size is not part of this horizon.

captureBeyondViewport:true is the CDP mechanism for the beyond-viewport pixels once the render pass is restored — discovery corrected this: no horizon-13 shim exists in source any more (it was removed after failing), so this must be built from scratch, not re-enabled.
The live head-to-head runs through the Claude Code chrome-bridge MCP against a real signed-in Chrome with the extension rebuilt and reloaded, per the horizon-2 real-Chrome closure decision.

'Bounded and reversible' is satisfied by disabling focus emulation and restoring pre-call state within the same withDebuggerSession scope; no cross-command state machine is needed. Discovery notes withDebuggerSession's own finally only detaches the debugger — it has no compensating-command pattern — so the enable/disable pair needs its own try/finally inside the run() closure.
If the probe refutes setFocusEmulationEnabled, the horizon replans (revise-phases) to either an alternative render mechanism or a deferral, rather than shipping full-page capture unverified.

getTabState reads chrome.tabs/chrome.windows state only and cannot detect a focus-emulation leak (a different Blink-internal layer) — the 'restore unfocused' contract must be verified by an explicit observation, not inferred from getTabState output.
risks: Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled may be experimental/unavailable in the target Chrome build, or may force Blink to treat the page as focused without actually resuming the compositor/render pass on a backgrounded tab — the same class of failure that killed captureBeyondViewport in horizon 13 — collapsing the horizon to a probe-only replan.

Even if it restores rendering, the encode of a multi-MB full-page PNG may not complete inside the 15s withDebuggerSession cap and could wedge the capture path until reloadTab, as captureBeyondViewport did in horizon 13.

Enabling focus emulation could visibly steal focus or alter the sandbox tab's activeTab/lifecycle state in a way that breaks the unfocused-tab invariant horizons 9-14 depend on, or that getTabState then misreports.

A crash/timeout between enabling focus emulation and disabling it could leave the sandbox tab permanently in an emulated-focus state or leave an orphaned debugger session (precedent: horizon 10 orphaned debugger on scrollPage hang).

The experimental CDP method is arguably outside the narrow 'CDP only for the captureVisibleTab gap' framing of the horizon-6 decision; treated here as covered by the horizon-9 broadening, but a reviewer may read it as reopening a closed decision.

The fresh-session live-Chrome head-to-head may hit the stale-MCP-catalog problem (h9/h11/h13) and require a retry in a post-rebuild session before the new full-page mode is callable, delaying closure.
device-scale-factor / emulation interaction may make returned full-page pixel dimensions diverge from measured CSS-pixel scrollHeight, weakening the mandatory cross-check (open h13 question).

The horizon-14 scale-only ladder may hit its give-up floor on large real full-page photographic captures often enough that full-page mode returns no image in practice, reviving pressure for a JPEG rung that is explicitly out of scope.
outOfScope: JPEG / quality downscale rungs — deferred by the horizon-14 decision because a JPEG rung forces a SOF0 dimension parser, data-URL prefix generalization, and format branching in mcp/server.ts.

Generalizing the screenshot size policy into a cross-tool result-size policy (readConsoleMessages / readNetworkRequests / executeScript / evaluatePage / findElement caps) — user scoped this as a separate future horizon.
Replacing per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach with a bounded persistent multi-command CDP session — user explicitly deferred; horizon-10 decision keeps per-command sessions.
Removing the dead active-tab code surface (queryActiveTab / captureVisibleTab / NO_ACTIVE_TAB / activeTab manifest permission) — user deferred; ~40 lines of test fallout not worth this horizon.
Virtualized / lazy-loaded content reads as a second consumer of the render primitive — the horizon ships exactly one consumer (full-page capture); this stays blocked.
Trusted CDP input (Input.dispatch* keyboard/click) as a consumer of the render primitive — still deferred; not a screenshot concern.
Un-scrolled below-the-fold single-element clip capture — a distinct deferred item behind the render prerequisite; this horizon does full-page only, not element mode changes.
Empirically re-measuring the true AI-client image-block reject size — the 1_200_000-char proxy from h13/h14 is carried unchanged.
Adding a distinct floor-exhaustion CaptureTabFailureReason — horizon-14 decision reuses 'too-large' with floor/attempts.
Any change to boky's own extension, BridgeRelayModule, or extension-mcp.mjs — the project never migrates boky onto the new tool (horizon-1 decision).
New page actions or touching page actions other than captureTab — the horizon stays confined to captureTab like h13/h14.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The work is browser-automation machinery — a CDP render-state primitive and a screenshot capture mode in a Chrome extension — with no business entities, rules, or workflows a domain expert would recognize.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: the dedicated Chrome tab the chrome-bridge extension drives, deliberately kept unfocused/backgrounded, sole target of every page action since horizon 6
the guarantee that the sandbox tab stays unfocused/backgrounded outside a capture; horizons 9-14 rely on it and this horizon must restore it after each render
Chrome's compositing/paint work for a tab; suspended on the backgrounded sandbox tab (horizon 10), which is why beyond-viewport and off-screen pixels come back blank
the new bounded, reversible mechanism this horizon builds — give the sandbox tab a real render pass for the duration of one capture, then restore the unfocused state

the candidate experimental CDP Emulation method that forces Blink to treat a page as focused/active regardless of OS window focus; the feasibility probe confirms or refutes that it restores the render pass

a live-Chrome test against the running extension, done before wiring anything permanent, that measures whether the candidate mechanism actually works (pattern from horizon 6 phase 0 and horizon 13 phase 0)
the one consumer shipped this horizon — a new value on captureTab's in-place mode field that captures the whole scrollable document via CDP captureBeyondViewport:true
horizon 14's scale-only PNG re-capture rungs (0.75/0.5/0.33) plus give-up floor and ceiling constant in page-actions.ts, reused unchanged for oversized full-page results
the per-command chrome.debugger attach/detach wrapper with a 15s CDP cap and a label union; the render primitive runs inside one of these, no persistent session
the set of files (PAGE_ACTIONS tuple, types maps, handler raw+guarded maps, tool-catalog, mcp/server.ts, README, count/list tests) that must change together so a tsc error catches drift

discoveryFindings.finding: There is currently NO captureBeyondViewport field anywhere in source. CaptureScreenshotOptions in debugger-ports.ts only has clip and scale; CaptureTabMode in protocol/types.ts is "viewport" | "element" only, with a doc comment stating full-page is 'deliberately not offered' because the horizon-13 probe proved it non-functional. The horizon-13 shim was removed after the probe failed — grep for captureBeyondViewport across src/ hits zero matches; it only survives in README.md's historical prose.
discoveryFindings.implication: A new full-page mode must add captureBeyondViewport support from scratch, not merely re-enable a shim.

discoveryFindings.area: parity surface for a new captureTab mode
discoveryFindings.finding: Adding a mode value touches: protocol/types.ts (CaptureTabMode union), page-actions.ts (resolveCaptureParams/ParsedCaptureParams, a new capture-path function, the captureTab raw handler dispatch), debugger-ports.ts (CaptureScreenshotOptions field + screenshotTab branch + doc comment), tool-catalog.ts (mode enum + description), mcp/server.ts (header doc comment), README.md, and tests. PAGE_ACTIONS stays 20 (in-place mode addition, not a new action).

withDebuggerSession<T>(tabId, label:"capturing"|"evaluating"|"scrolling", run, timeoutMs=CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=15000). Its own finally ALWAYS detaches on every exit path, but there is NO existing 'undo mid-session' pattern — the wrapper never sends a compensating CDP command.
discoveryFindings.implication: An enable-focus-emulation -> capture -> disable sequence must run as one run() closure with its OWN try/finally around the CDP calls to guarantee the disable fires even if capture throws.

discoveryFindings.finding: Grepping src/ for Emulation finds zero CDP command sites; only Page.captureScreenshot, Runtime.evaluate, and Input.dispatchMouseEvent are ever sent. Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled is unused/untested today.

captureResultWithLadder(initialDataUrl, recapture, clipped) delegates to captureDownscaleLadder(recapture, clipped) walking SCREENSHOT_DOWNSCALE_LADDER_SCALES=[0.75,0.5,0.33], floor=0.33, ceiling MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS=1_200_000. It is called from BOTH captureViewport and captureElement today — a shared, mode-agnostic helper.
discoveryFindings.implication: A new full-page mode can reuse captureResultWithLadder/captureDownscaleLadder unchanged by supplying its own recapture(scale) closure.

discoveryFindings.finding: readPngDimensions(dataUrl) and captureUnavailableOutcome(error) are already mode-agnostic and directly reusable by a full-page path.

In screenshotTab, when options.clip is absent and options.scale is present, it reads the layout viewport via Runtime.evaluate and SYNTHESIZES a clip — there is no direct 'scale without a synthesized clip' path today. A full-page recapture-at-scale needs its own branch sending captureBeyondViewport:true with no synthesized clip.

actions.unit.test.ts (length 20 + ordered tuple) and tool-catalog.unit.test.ts (length 20 + names) are unaffected by an in-place mode addition. resolveCaptureParams's literal error string hardcoding the two-value mode list WILL need updating.
installStubDebugger(sendCommand?) returns {attachSpy,detachSpy,sendCommandSpy,addListenerSpy,fireDetach}; existing tests assert exact Page.captureScreenshot params objects passed to sendCommandSpy.

fakeDebugger(overrides) stubs captureScreenshot/evaluate/scroll. pngB64(width,height) builds a valid PNG with a real IHDR. captureTab({mode:'element'|'viewport'}) are the call shapes; a full-page test calls captureTab({mode:'full-page'}).

discoveryFindings.area: sandbox tab creation and unfocused invariant
discoveryFindings.finding: chromeSandboxTabPorts() creates the tab via chrome.tabs.create({active:false}) — load-bearing. NO code ever calls chrome.tabs.update/windows.update to focus the sandbox tab. getTabState is purely read-only and reports sandboxTabActive from chrome.tabs/chrome.windows state, never document.hasFocus() or any CDP Emulation state.
discoveryFindings.implication: Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled only affects Blink's internal document-focus state, NOT chrome.tabs.active/chrome.windows.focused — getTabState would likely NOT detect a focus-emulation leak at all; the render primitive's 'restore unfocused' contract must be verified by an explicit disable + observation, not by asserting on getTabState output.

discoveryFindings.finding: DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS=200_000; MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS=1_000_000; MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS=1_200_000; SCREENSHOT_DOWNSCALE_LADDER_SCALES=[0.75,0.5,0.33] as const; SCREENSHOT_DOWNSCALE_FLOOR_SCALE=0.33 — top of page-actions.ts, each with a unit test tying the floor to the ladder's last element.
extension/manifest.json already declares the debugger permission and host_permissions <all_urls> — no manifest change needed for an additional Emulation.* CDP command.
npm run verify runs tsc --noEmit && eslint . --max-warnings 0 && vitest run in sequence — no config changes needed to add tests.

requiredMaterials.name: Chrome DevTools Protocol Emulation domain reference (setFocusEmulationEnabled)
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Nothing in the repo has ever called an Emulation.* CDP method and the feasibility probe must confirm or refute this before wiring anything permanent — need the official method signature, parameter shape, and any documented caveats about experimental/deprecated status.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Fetch chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol (Emulation domain, setFocusEmulationEnabled) via WebFetch; cross-check against the actual DevTools protocol version reported by the target Chrome build.

requiredMaterials.name: Live running Chrome instance with the chrome-bridge extension loaded and reachable
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The feasibility probe and the mandatory fresh-session head-to-head both require exercising the real chrome.debugger/CDP stack against a real backgrounded sandbox tab — this cannot be simulated in vitest.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Build/reload the chrome-bridge extension unpacked in a real signed-in Chrome profile and drive it through the project's own MCP/bridge connection; be prepared for the stale-MCP-catalog-after-rebuild issue noted in prior horizons.

requiredMaterials.name: Test page with content taller/wider than the viewport
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Verifying captureBeyondViewport pixels are non-blank and cross-checking returned dimensions against measured scrollHeight/scrollWidth requires a known scrollable document to probe against.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Use or author a simple local/static HTML fixture with deterministic, visually distinct content well beyond one viewport height.

phases.name: Probe focus-emulation render restore in sandbox tab
phases.goal: Prove, against real signed-in Chrome and before any permanent wiring, whether CDP Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true) on the unfocused sandbox tab restores enough of a render pass that a subsequent Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) returns non-blank beyond-viewport pixels within the 15s withDebuggerSession cap.
phases.rationale: Discovery found zero Emulation.* CDP call sites anywhere in source, and the horizon-13 captureBeyondViewport shim was removed from source/dist after its own probe proved it non-functional on the unfocused sandbox tab without a render-restoring mechanism. This candidate mechanism must be confirmed live before any port function, capture mode, or parity-surface change is built around it, mirroring the h6 phase-0 / h13 phase-0 feasibility-gate pattern.
changes: From a fresh MCP session against a real scrollable test page loaded in the sandbox tab, send Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:true}) then Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) over the same chrome.debugger attachment and inspect the returned PNG for non-blank pixels beyond the initial viewport
Compare the returned image height against a CDP evaluatePage document scroll-height measurement of the same page, and record the wall-clock duration against the 15s withDebuggerSession cap
Send Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:false}) and confirm the debugger detaches cleanly with no orphaned session left on the tab
Record a dated finding in discoveries.md with the measured numbers and timing, ending in one explicit proceed/replan verdict
inputs: discovery: zero Emulation.* usage anywhere, h13 captureBeyondViewport shim removed after failing without a render primitive
live signed-in Chrome instance with the extension loaded and relay running
phases.expectedResult: A dated finding in discoveries.md stating, with measured numbers and timing, whether setFocusEmulationEnabled restores a real render pass for captureBeyondViewport in the unfocused sandbox tab, ending in an explicit proceed/replan verdict.
phases.compensation: If the finding is negative, stop and REPLAN the horizon rather than building the render primitive, the full-page capture mode, or any parity-surface wiring; the horizon may close here as a probe-only result with the negative finding recorded.

rubric.label: Dated finding recorded with measured numbers
rubric.ruleStatement: discoveries.md must contain a dated entry for this probe with concrete measured values, not a narrative summary.
passCriteria: discoveries.md has a new entry dated 2026-09-04 (or the actual run date) identifiable as the focus-emulation render-restore probe
Entry states the returned PNG's pixel dimensions (width x height) actually captured
Entry states the document scroll-height measured via CDP evaluatePage for comparison against the captured height
Entry states the wall-clock duration of the full probe sequence in seconds or milliseconds
Entry states whether non-blank pixels were found beyond the initial viewport, described concretely, not just asserted
failureExamples: Entry says 'ran the probe, screenshot looked full-page' with no dimensions, scroll-height, or timing numbers recorded
Entry records the PNG dimensions but omits the scroll-height comparison, so 'beyond viewport' can't actually be verified from the written numbers
Entry only pastes a raw JSON response dump without stating the derived width/height/scroll-height/duration values in prose

rubric.label: Explicit proceed or replan verdict
rubric.ruleStatement: The finding must end in one unambiguous verdict word/phrase, not an open question or hedge.
passCriteria: Entry contains a clearly labeled verdict line, e.g. 'Verdict: PROCEED' or 'Verdict: REPLAN'
The verdict is a direct logical consequence of the numbers reported earlier in the same entry
No conditional/hedged language substitutes for the verdict
failureExamples: Entry ends with 'results were promising, worth exploring further' instead of a stated verdict
Entry states a verdict but it contradicts the reported numbers
Entry gives two conflicting verdicts in different places

rubric.label: Probe followed the specified CDP sequence over one attachment
rubric.ruleStatement: The finding must show the exact sequence — enable focus emulation, capture beyond-viewport, disable focus emulation — was run over a single chrome.debugger attachment on the sandbox tab, not a proxy or partial substitute.
passCriteria: Entry names the actual CDP calls issued: Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:true}), Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}), and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:false})
Entry confirms these ran within one chrome.debugger session/attachment on the sandbox tab (not a fresh tab, not a manually-focused tab)
Entry identifies the test page used and confirms it is genuinely scrollable/taller than viewport, stating its actual scroll height
failureExamples: Entry reports a screenshot captured after manually focusing the Chrome window instead of via setFocusEmulationEnabled on the backgrounded tab — which would prove focus fixes it, not that the CDP call does

Entry tests against a short test page whose full content already fits in one viewport, so a 'non-blank full page' result cannot distinguish real beyond-viewport rendering from an ordinary in-viewport capture
Entry never states which chrome.debugger session was used or whether attach happened once, leaving it ambiguous whether enable/capture/disable used the same attachment

rubric.label: Debugger detaches cleanly with no orphaned session
rubric.ruleStatement: The finding must explicitly confirm the debugger session was detached after the probe and no session was left attached to the tab.
passCriteria: Entry states focus emulation was explicitly disabled before detach
Entry states the chrome.debugger session was detached and names how this was confirmed
Entry confirms the unfocused-tab invariant held after the probe
failureExamples: Entry says 'detach() was called' but never confirms the tab's actual post-probe state, so an exception mid-sequence leaving an orphaned attachment would go unnoticed
Entry confirms detach but never checks whether setFocusEmulationEnabled(false) actually took effect before detaching
Entry omits any mention of teardown at all, only covering the capture result

rubric.label: Timing measured against the 15s withDebuggerSession cap
rubric.ruleStatement: The finding must report the probe's actual wall-clock duration and state explicitly whether it fits within the 15s cap this mechanism must eventually run inside.
passCriteria: Entry reports a specific elapsed time for the full attach-enable-capture-disable-detach sequence
Entry explicitly compares that number to the 15s cap and states margin or overage
If the probe used any wait/settle delay before capturing, that delay is itemized separately
failureExamples: Entry reports total time but never states whether it is under or over 15s, leaving the reader to do the comparison
Entry's timing includes an unstated ad-hoc sleep/wait added to make the capture work, which would make the true production duration unknown even though the measured number was under 15s

phases.healerHint: If the finding is missing measured numbers or an explicit verdict, don't re-run the probe from scratch — first check whether the raw CDP responses were captured anywhere and just backfill the derived width/height/scroll-height/duration/verdict computation into discoveries.md.

phases.name: Add reversible full-page capture to debugger-ports
phases.goal: Add a new DebuggerPorts capability that, within one withDebuggerSession session, enables CDP focus emulation on the sandbox tab, captures a beyond-viewport PNG via Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}), and disables focus emulation in its own try/finally around the capture step so the compensating disable fires on every exit path including a thrown capture error.
phases.rationale: Discovery: CaptureScreenshotOptions today only has clip/scale (no captureBeyondViewport field) and its doc comment explicitly states full-page is not offered; withDebuggerSession's own finally only detaches the debugger, it has no built-in compensating-command pattern, so the enable/disable pair must be its own try/finally inside the run() closure to guarantee reversibility even when capture throws or times out.
changes: Add captureBeyondViewport?:boolean to CaptureScreenshotOptions and a params-building branch in screenshotTab that sends Page.captureScreenshot({format:'png', captureBeyondViewport:true}) with no synthesized clip

Add a new exported port function (e.g. captureFullPageScreenshot(tabId, options)) that runs inside withDebuggerSession under a new label, sends Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:true}), then in a try/finally calls screenshotTab with captureBeyondViewport:true and, in finally, unconditionally sends Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:false})
Update the DebuggerPorts.captureScreenshot doc comment that currently states full-page is NOT offered

Add unit tests via installStubDebugger asserting the exact CDP command sequence (enable, capture, disable) on a successful capture, and asserting disable is STILL sent when the capture step's sendCommand rejects
inputs: discovery: CaptureScreenshotOptions clip/scale-only, zero Emulation.* usage, withDebuggerSession label union and detach-only finally
phases.expectedResult: A new captureFullPageScreenshot port function in debugger-ports.ts whose unit tests prove Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(false) is sent on every exit path, including when the capture step throws.
phases.compensation: Revert the new port function, the CaptureScreenshotOptions field, and the doc-comment change in one commit; nothing else consumes this file yet so rollback is isolated.

rubric.label: Focus emulation is disabled on every exit path
rubric.ruleStatement: The enable/disable pair for Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled must be wrapped in its own try/finally around the capture step, independent of withDebuggerSession's detach-only finally, so the disable command is sent regardless of whether the capture succeeds, throws, or the session subsequently fails to detach.
passCriteria: screenshotTab/capture call sits inside a try block whose finally unconditionally sends Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled({enabled:false})

The disable command is sent even when Page.captureScreenshot (or any command between enable and capture) rejects/throws — verified by a unit test that stubs the capture command to reject and asserts the disable call still fired
Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(false) is not conditioned on the enable call having previously succeeded
No new code path exists that can leave focus emulation enabled after captureFullPageScreenshot returns or throws
failureExamples: A developer wraps the whole withDebuggerSession callback in one try/finally at the outer level, which looks equivalent but is dropped when someone later adds an early-return before the capture step, silently un-guarding it
The disable call is placed as the last statement in the happy path instead of in finally, so it is skipped when captureScreenshot throws
Disable is sent but with the wrong tabId/session target, so the compensating command silently no-ops on the real tab

rubric.label: Unit tests assert the exact CDP command sequence
rubric.ruleStatement: installStubDebugger-based unit tests must assert, in order, that Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true) precedes Page.captureScreenshot with captureBeyondViewport:true, which precedes Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(false), for both the success case and the capture-throws case.
passCriteria: debugger-ports.unit.test.ts contains a test that captures the stub's recorded command list and asserts enable, capture, disable appear in that exact order for a successful call
A second test stubs the capture command to reject and asserts the recorded commands still include the disable call
The capture command's params object is asserted to include captureBeyondViewport:true and no synthesized clip field
Tests fail (red) if the disable call is removed or reordered
failureExamples: Test asserts sendCommand was called 3 times total but never checks which commands or their order, so a bug that sends disable-enable-capture would still pass
Test only covers the happy path; the throw-case test exists but only asserts the outer promise rejects, without inspecting whether disable was actually sent
Test asserts captureBeyondViewport:true is sent but doesn't check that clip is omitted

rubric.label: Screenshot params match full-page capture semantics
rubric.ruleStatement: CaptureScreenshotOptions gains captureBeyondViewport as an optional boolean, and screenshotTab's params-building branch sends format:'png', captureBeyondViewport:true with no clip field synthesized, leaving existing clip/scale call sites unaffected.
passCriteria: CaptureScreenshotOptions in debugger-ports.ts has a new optional captureBeyondViewport?:boolean field with no change to the existing clip/scale fields' types
The new branch in screenshotTab omits any clip object when captureBeyondViewport is true
Existing call sites that pass clip/scale (horizon 14's downscale ladder) are unmodified in behavior
format:'png' is explicit in the sent params
failureExamples: Developer adds captureBeyondViewport but still builds a clip from the current viewport dimensions 'just in case', defeating beyond-viewport capture on tall pages
The new field is typed as boolean (not optional), forcing every existing call site to pass captureBeyondViewport:false, silently expanding the parity surface beyond this phase's declared file list

rubric.label: Doc comment no longer contradicts the shipped capability
rubric.ruleStatement: The DebuggerPorts.captureScreenshot doc comment that currently asserts full-page capture is not offered must be corrected to describe the new captureFullPageScreenshot port and its scope, not merely deleted.
passCriteria: The stale sentence stating full-page/beyond-viewport capture is not offered is removed from captureScreenshot's doc comment
A doc comment on the new captureFullPageScreenshot function states it enables focus emulation for the duration of one capture and disables it afterward
The updated doc comment does not claim capabilities beyond what phase 1 ships
Grep for the phrase describing full-page as unsupported returns no remaining matches in debugger-ports.ts
failureExamples: Developer deletes the stale sentence but adds no replacement documentation on the new function
Doc comment is copy-pasted under captureScreenshot's existing JSDoc block instead of attached to captureFullPageScreenshot

rubric.label: New port function respects withDebuggerSession's session/label contract and typed error handling
rubric.ruleStatement: captureFullPageScreenshot must run under a new, distinct withDebuggerSession label (not reuse an existing capture label), pass tabId through the same attach/detach machinery, and any error path must preserve typed error information rather than swallowing or re-throwing as a generic/any-typed error.
passCriteria: A new string literal label is added to withDebuggerSession's label union specifically for full-page capture
captureFullPageScreenshot's signature and thrown/rejected error types satisfy the repo's no-any / no-non-null-assertion rules (tsc/eslint pass)
If the enable or capture command rejects, the original error propagates out after the finally's disable has run
No new chrome.debugger.* call bypasses the existing attach/detach wrapper
failureExamples: Developer reuses the existing 'screenshot' label for the new function since 'it's basically the same operation', muddying the parity surface
The finally block's disable call itself can throw; that secondary error replaces/swallows the original capture error instead of the original still propagating

phases.healerHint: If the capture-throws unit test still passes when the disable call is deleted, the enable/disable pair isn't in its own try/finally around the capture step — move it there rather than relying on withDebuggerSession's outer finally, which only detaches the debugger.

phases.name: Add full-page mode runtime wiring in captureTab
phases.goal: Add a new full-page value to captureTab's in-place mode field and wire it in page-actions.ts to the new captureFullPageScreenshot port, reusing horizon 14's scale-only downscale ladder unchanged for oversized results.
phases.rationale: Discovery: adding a mode value touches protocol/types.ts's CaptureTabMode union, page-actions.ts's resolveCaptureParams/dispatch, tool-catalog.ts's mode enum and description, mcp/server.ts's header doc comment, and README in lockstep so a missed one is a tsc/test error; this phase ships the runtime half of that parity surface (types + dispatch + ladder reuse), with the surface-facing half (tool-catalog/docs) split into a following phase so each stays independently reviewable as one deliverable. captureResultWithLadder/captureDownscaleLadder are already mode-agnostic helpers reusable via a full-page recapture(scale) closure with zero ladder-code changes, and PAGE_ACTIONS stays 20 since this is an in-place mode addition, not a new action.
changes: Add the new mode value to CaptureTabMode in protocol/types.ts and update the CaptureTabParams doc comment

In page-actions.ts, extend resolveCaptureParams/ParsedCaptureParams to accept and validate the new mode (updating the hardcoded two-value mode-list error string), add a captureFullPage function mirroring captureViewport's pattern — initial shot via captureFullPageScreenshot(tabId), recapture=(scale)=>captureFullPageScreenshot(tabId,{scale}) — passing both into the existing captureResultWithLadder unchanged, then dispatch the new mode in the captureTab raw handler's mode switch

Add unit test coverage in page-actions.unit.test.ts for resolveCaptureParams accepting the new mode plus captureTab({mode:'full-page'}) exercising the ladder (appliedScale/attempts on success, floor/attempts on too-large)
inputs: discovery: parity-surface file list and resolveCaptureParams hardcoded mode-list string
phases.expectedResult: captureTab accepts and dispatches full-page mode with ladder reuse proven by unit tests.

rubric.label: resolveCaptureParams and mode dispatch correctly extended
rubric.ruleStatement: resolveCaptureParams/ParsedCaptureParams accept and validate the new mode value, the mode-list error string is updated to name all three modes, and the captureTab raw handler's mode switch dispatches full-page to captureFullPage.
passCriteria: resolveCaptureParams accepts 'full-page' as a valid value for the mode field without throwing
the mode-validation error message is updated in source to list all three valid modes
the captureTab handler's switch/if-chain over mode has an explicit branch invoking captureFullPage for the new mode, not falling through to a default/viewport case
calling captureTab with an unsupported string still throws the same validation error naming the three valid values
failureExamples: the switch statement adds a case for 'full-page' that calls captureFullPage correctly, but the hardcoded error string in resolveCaptureParams still lists only 'viewport' and 'element'

'full-page' is added to the TypeScript union type so it compiles, but the runtime validation in resolveCaptureParams was never updated, so passing mode:'full-page' at runtime throws the old two-value error

rubric.label: PAGE_ACTIONS count stays 20 (in-place mode addition, not a new action)
rubric.ruleStatement: This phase must not add a new entry to PAGE_ACTIONS or any equivalent action registry — full-page is a mode value on the existing captureTab action.
passCriteria: count of PAGE_ACTIONS shows exactly 20 entries after the change, same as before the phase
no new exported action name such as 'captureFullPageScreenshot' or 'captureTabFullPage' appears in the action registry/dispatch table used by tool-catalog.ts's top-level action list
this phase's change is confined to CaptureTabMode/page-actions.ts, not a new top-level tool/action entry
failureExamples: a well-intentioned implementation adds a distinct 'captureFullPageTab' entry to PAGE_ACTIONS alongside updating the mode field, bringing the count to 21

rubric.label: Downscale ladder reused unchanged, not reimplemented
rubric.ruleStatement: The full-page capture path must call the existing captureResultWithLadder/downscale-ladder helper(s) from horizon 14 with a recapture(scale) closure, with zero new ladder logic introduced in this phase's diff.
passCriteria: page-actions.ts's captureFullPage function calls the existing captureResultWithLadder rather than defining its own loop over scales
the recapture callback passed for full-page is literally '(scale) => captureFullPageScreenshot(tabId, { scale })' (or equivalent), mirroring captureViewport's existing pattern
no new constant array, loop, or module duplicating SCREENSHOT_DOWNSCALE_LADDER_SCALES / floor logic appears anywhere in the diff
the unit test for captureTab({mode:'full-page'}) exercising the ladder asserts appliedScale/attempts on a success path and floor/attempts on a too-large path
failureExamples: captureFullPage hand-rolls its own while-loop trying successive scale factors until the PNG is under the size limit — a duplicate, divergent implementation of the ladder
a second, near-identical ladder-rung constant array is defined locally in page-actions.ts for full-page mode 'to be safe', creating two sources of truth

rubric.label: page-actions unit tests cover both ladder outcomes for full-page mode
rubric.ruleStatement: page-actions.unit.test.ts must contain new, passing test cases exercising the full-page mode value, including a resolveCaptureParams acceptance test, a ladder-success test, and a ladder-floor test.
passCriteria: page-actions.unit.test.ts has a test asserting resolveCaptureParams accepts mode:'full-page'
page-actions.unit.test.ts has a test calling captureTab({mode:'full-page', ...}) that asserts appliedScale and attempts fields on a normal-size result
page-actions.unit.test.ts has a test calling captureTab({mode:'full-page', ...}) with an oversized result that asserts the floor scale and attempts are reported when the ladder bottoms out
npm run verify passes green for tools/chrome-bridge with these tests included
failureExamples: a test calling captureTab({mode:'full-page'}) merely asserts it does not throw, without checking appliedScale/attempts/floor behavior, so a broken ladder wiring would still pass this test
resolveCaptureParams acceptance test is missing entirely, so a mode-validation regression is invisible in this phase's tests

phases.healerHint: If resolveCaptureParams rejects mode:'full-page' at runtime even though CaptureTabMode compiles, the type union was updated but the runtime validation/error string was not — fix the validation function, not the type.

phases.name: Update MCP tool catalog and docs for full-page mode
phases.goal: Update the MCP tool schema (tool-catalog.ts) and documentation (mcp/server.ts doc comment, README.md) so they advertise the new full-page captureTab mode consistently with the runtime wiring shipped in the prior phase.
phases.rationale: Discovery: adding a mode value touches protocol/types.ts, page-actions.ts, tool-catalog.ts, mcp/server.ts, and README in lockstep so a missed one is a tsc/test error or, worse, an MCP schema that silently disagrees with what the runtime actually accepts; this phase ships the surface-facing half of that parity surface (catalog + docs), following the runtime wiring phase, so each stays independently reviewable as one deliverable.
changes: Update tool-catalog.ts's captureTab mode enum array and description to include the new value
Update mcp/server.ts's header doc comment, which currently states captureTab only supports viewport/element modes, to include full-page
Update README's captureTab section, replacing the 'full-page capture is not offered' paragraph and the mode bullet list
Add a unit test in tool-catalog.unit.test.ts asserting the captureTab tool schema's mode enum includes 'full-page'
inputs: phase-2 full-page mode runtime wiring (resolveCaptureParams, captureFullPage dispatch)
phases.expectedResult: The MCP tool schema and docs advertise full-page mode consistently with the runtime.

rubric.label: Catalog and docs surfaces updated consistently
rubric.ruleStatement: Every file listed in filesAffected (tool-catalog.ts, tool-catalog.unit.test.ts, mcp/server.ts, README.md) must show a change that reflects the new full-page mode, matching the runtime wiring shipped in the prior phase.
passCriteria: git diff shows non-trivial changes in all four filesAffected paths: tool-catalog.ts, tool-catalog.unit.test.ts, server.ts, README.md
tool-catalog.ts's captureTab mode enum array literally contains the new full-page value and its description text mentions it
mcp/server.ts's header doc comment no longer states captureTab supports only viewport/element modes
README.md's captureTab section no longer contains the old 'full-page capture is not offered' sentence and its mode bullet list includes the new mode
grep for the new mode string returns hits in all four files
failureExamples: tool-catalog.ts's enum array is left with only the old two values, so the MCP tool schema silently rejects the new mode despite the runtime dispatcher accepting it
README.md still contains the 'full-page capture is not offered' sentence, left over from before this phase
server.ts's header doc comment is not touched, so it still documents captureTab as viewport/element only

rubric.label: tool-catalog unit tests assert the schema advertises full-page mode
rubric.ruleStatement: tool-catalog.unit.test.ts must contain a new, passing test case asserting the captureTab tool schema's mode enum includes 'full-page'.
passCriteria: tool-catalog.unit.test.ts has a test asserting the captureTab tool schema's mode enum includes 'full-page'
the test asserts the literal string 'full-page' is present, not merely that the enum array length increased
npm run verify passes green for tools/chrome-bridge with this test included
failureExamples: tool-catalog.unit.test.ts checks the enum array length increased but never asserts the literal string 'full-page' is present

rubric.label: Advertised schema matches the modes the runtime actually dispatches
rubric.ruleStatement: The mode values advertised in tool-catalog.ts and described in README.md/server.ts must exactly match the mode values resolveCaptureParams/the captureTab dispatcher accept at runtime — no advertised mode lacking runtime support, and no runtime-supported mode left undocumented.
passCriteria: tool-catalog.ts's mode enum array contains exactly the same mode values as resolveCaptureParams validates (viewport, element, full-page) — no more, no fewer
README.md's mode bullet list names all three modes and none that don't exist
server.ts's doc comment lists the same three modes
failureExamples: tool-catalog.ts advertises a 'full-page' mode but the doc comment in server.ts still lists only two modes, leaving the documentation internally inconsistent
README.md invents a fourth mode name that was never wired at runtime

phases.healerHint: If a catalog/docs file was skipped, grep the diff for the new mode string across all four filesAffected paths and patch whichever file is missing it before touching anything else.

phases.name: Run live-Chrome full-page capture head-to-head
phases.goal: In a fresh post-rebuild MCP session against real signed-in Chrome, capture a real beyond-viewport page in full-page mode on the unfocused sandbox tab, cross-check the returned pixel dimensions against measured scrollHeight/scrollWidth, confirm the sandbox tab is unfocused again afterward, and record a dated finding in discoveries.md.
phases.rationale: Stage1 success criterion 6 mandates this closing check. Discovery notes getTabState only reads chrome.tabs/chrome.windows state and cannot detect a focus-emulation leak (a different Blink-internal layer), so the unfocused-invariant confirmation must be an explicit post-run observation rather than inferred from getTabState output.
changes: Rebuild and reload the chrome-bridge extension, start a fresh MCP session (retry once if the tool catalog is stale post-rebuild, per prior-horizon precedent), and navigate the sandbox tab to a real page with content well beyond one viewport
Call captureTab in full-page mode and record the returned image pixel dimensions

Measure the same page's scrollHeight/scrollWidth via the existing evaluate/page-text primitive and cross-check against the returned dimensions, reconciling device-pixel-ratio if the two differ in units

Confirm the sandbox tab is unfocused again after the capture returns and that no debugger attachment or focus-emulation state was left behind, and record a dated Verified or honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING finding in discoveries.md
inputs: phase-3 MCP tool schema and docs advertising full-page mode
live signed-in Chrome instance with the rebuilt extension loaded and relay running
test page with content taller/wider than the viewport
phases.expectedResult: A dated finding in discoveries.md recording a real full-page capture's returned dimensions cross-checked against measured scrollHeight/scrollWidth and confirming the sandbox tab is unfocused afterward, or an honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note naming the blocker.

rubric.label: Pixel dimensions cross-checked against measured scroll size
rubric.ruleStatement: The captured image's pixel dimensions must be reconciled against independently measured page scrollHeight/scrollWidth, with the arithmetic shown, not merely asserted.
passCriteria: discoveries.md shows the raw captureTab output dimensions (width x height in px) for the full-page capture
discoveries.md shows the raw scrollHeight/scrollWidth values measured via the evaluate/page-text primitive, from the same page load
An explicit reconciliation line shows how the two numbers relate (e.g. capturedHeight / scrollHeight ≈ devicePixelRatio, with the actual ratio computed and named)
If a discrepancy exists, the entry states it in pixels/percent and either explains it as a device-pixel-ratio unit gap or flags it as unresolved
failureExamples: Entry says 'full-page screenshot captured successfully, dimensions look correct' with no numbers
Entry lists both numbers but never states or computes the DPR relationship, so a 2x-scaled screen would silently read as a mismatch and go unremarked
Only the captureTab dimensions are recorded; scrollHeight/scrollWidth were never independently measured

rubric.label: Stale post-rebuild MCP catalog handling reported honestly
rubric.ruleStatement: If the MCP tool catalog was stale after the rebuild/reload and required a retry, discoveries.md must say so explicitly with what was observed and what the retry fixed; if no retry was needed, the entry must say that plainly.
passCriteria: discoveries.md contains an explicit sentence addressing whether a stale-catalog retry occurred
If a retry occurred, the entry names the concrete symptom and confirms the second session's catalog included the new mode before capture was attempted
No language implies success was assumed without confirming the tool was actually present in the session that produced the capture
failureExamples: discoveries.md never mentions the MCP session/catalog state at all, jumping straight to capture results
Entry says 'had to restart the MCP session' without saying why, or without confirming the retried session actually had the new full-page mode available before capturing

rubric.label: Sandbox tab confirmed unfocused and clean after capture
rubric.ruleStatement: After the capture call returns, the finding must record an explicit, separately-performed check that the sandbox tab is unfocused again and that no debugger attachment or focus-emulation state was left behind — not an inference from the capture succeeding.
passCriteria: discoveries.md records a post-capture check performed after captureTab returned, with its actual observed result quoted or paraphrased with values
The entry states explicitly that no chrome.debugger session remained attached to the sandbox tab after the capture
The entry explicitly acknowledges the discovery-note caveat that getTabState cannot see Blink-internal focus-emulation state, and states what was actually done to gain confidence on that point
The confirmation appears as a distinct step/paragraph after the capture step, not folded into the capture success claim
failureExamples: Entry says 'sandbox tab returned to its normal unfocused state after the capture' with no described check and no value
Entry checks getTabState post-capture and reports it looks unfocused, but never mentions the known getTabState blind spot for focus-emulation leakage, implying a false all-clear
No mention of debugger detachment at all

rubric.label: Dated finding recorded, including honest blocker fallback if run could not complete
rubric.ruleStatement: discoveries.md must gain one dated entry for this phase that is either a complete Verified finding per the above dimensions, or an explicit MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING entry naming the concrete blocker — never a vague or omitted entry.
passCriteria: A new entry exists in discoveries.md with today's date and a clear phase/topic label
The entry is tagged either Verified (all sub-checks above present) or MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING
If MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING, the entry names the specific blocker rather than a generic 'could not verify'
The entry is additive — prior discoveries.md content remains intact and unmodified
failureExamples: A Verified entry is written but the run actually stalled partway and that gap is not disclosed
No entry was added to discoveries.md at all despite the task claiming completion
Entry exists but is undated or dated ambiguously

phases.healerHint: If captureTab's full-page mode call fails or times out right after the rebuild, first retry with a freshly-started MCP session before touching any capture code — the failure is very likely the known stale-tool-catalog issue, not a real regression.

successCriteria: Done means all hold: (1) a live-Chrome feasibility probe against the running extension has recorded in discoveries.md whether Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled actually restores a render pass on the unfocused sandbox tab enough for captureBeyondViewport to return non-blank beyond-viewport pixels within the 15s withDebuggerSession cap — and if it refutes that, the horizon replans rather than wiring anything permanent; (2) a render-the-tab primitive exists that is bounded and reversible, leaving no orphaned debugger session or lingering focus-emulation after it returns; (3) captureTab gains a full-page mode via the existing in-place mode field with PAGE_ACTIONS still 20, across the full parity surface; (4) an oversized full-page result is driven down horizon 14's existing scale-only PNG ladder unchanged; (5) tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and vitest all pass for tools/chrome-bridge; (6) a mandatory fresh-session live-Chrome head-to-head captures a real beyond-viewport page, cross-checks pixel dimensions, confirms the tab is unfocused again, and is recorded dated in discoveries.md; (7) boky's extension, bridge, and verify pipeline keep passing unchanged.

Probe focus-emulation render restore in sandbox tab: A dated finding in discoveries.md stating, with measured numbers and timing, whether setFocusEmulationEnabled restores a real render pass for captureBeyondViewport in the unfocused sandbox tab, ending in an explicit proceed/replan verdict.

Add reversible full-page capture to debugger-ports: A new captureFullPageScreenshot port function in debugger-ports.ts whose unit tests prove Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(false) is sent on every exit path, including when the capture step throws.
Add full-page mode runtime wiring in captureTab: captureTab accepts and dispatches full-page mode with ladder reuse proven by unit tests.
Update MCP tool catalog and docs for full-page mode: the MCP tool schema and docs advertise full-page mode consistently with the runtime.

Run live-Chrome full-page capture head-to-head: A dated finding in discoveries.md recording a real full-page capture's returned dimensions cross-checked against measured scrollHeight/scrollWidth and confirming the sandbox tab is unfocused afterward, or an honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note naming the blocker.
deferred: JPEG / quality downscale rungs — deferred by the horizon-14 decision because a JPEG rung forces a SOF0 dimension parser, data-URL prefix generalization, and format branching in mcp/server.ts.

Generalizing the screenshot size policy into a cross-tool result-size policy (readConsoleMessages / readNetworkRequests / executeScript / evaluatePage / findElement caps) — user scoped this as a separate future horizon.
Replacing per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach with a bounded persistent multi-command CDP session — user explicitly deferred; horizon-10 decision keeps per-command sessions.
Removing the dead active-tab code surface (queryActiveTab / captureVisibleTab / NO_ACTIVE_TAB / activeTab manifest permission) — user deferred; ~40 lines of test fallout not worth this horizon.
Virtualized / lazy-loaded content reads as a second consumer of the render primitive — the horizon ships exactly one consumer (full-page capture); this stays blocked.
Trusted CDP input (Input.dispatch* keyboard/click) as a consumer of the render primitive — still deferred; not a screenshot concern.
Un-scrolled below-the-fold single-element clip capture — a distinct deferred item behind the render prerequisite; this horizon does full-page only, not element mode changes.
Empirically re-measuring the true AI-client image-block reject size — the 1_200_000-char proxy from h13/h14 is carried unchanged.
Adding a distinct floor-exhaustion CaptureTabFailureReason — horizon-14 decision reuses 'too-large' with floor/attempts.
Any change to boky's own extension, BridgeRelayModule, or extension-mcp.mjs — the project never migrates boky onto the new tool (horizon-1 decision).
New page actions or touching page actions other than captureTab — the horizon stays confined to captureTab like h13/h14.

JPEG/quality downscale rung for oversized full-page results — explicitly out of scope per the h14 decision; the h14 scale-only ladder is reused unchanged and this horizon's success criteria reuse the 'too-large' reason with no new failure member

Generalizing the render-the-tab primitive into a reusable abstraction serving a second consumer — full-page capture is the single consumer this horizon ships; virtualized/lazy-content reads and trusted CDP input stay blocked behind the same primitive but are not built for in this horizon
Un-scrolled below-the-fold single-element clip capture changes — a distinct deferred item behind the render prerequisite; this horizon ships full-page mode only, not element-mode changes

Replacing per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach with a persistent multi-command CDP session — explicitly deferred by the horizon-10 decision, unrelated to shipping one bounded reversible primitive
Removing the dead active-tab code surface (queryActiveTab/captureVisibleTab/NO_ACTIVE_TAB/activeTab permission) — user-deferred cleanup unrelated to this horizon's deliverable
Generalizing the screenshot size policy into a cross-tool result-size policy for other page actions — user scoped this as a separate future horizon
Empirically re-measuring the true AI-client image-block reject size behind the 1_200_000-char ceiling — the h13/h14 proxy constant is carried forward unchanged
Adding a distinct floor-exhaustion CaptureTabFailureReason for full-page — reuses 'too-large' with floor/attempts per the h14 decision, a new reason member would be unused surface
